ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$. $OE$ bisects $\angle BOC$, $OF\perp OE$, and $\angle AOD=66^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle BOF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle AOD = 66^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BOC = \angle AOD = 66^\circ$,\\
since OE bisects $\angle BOC$,\\
therefore $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{2} \angle BOC = 33^\circ$,\\
since OF is perpendicular to OE,\\
therefore $\angle EOF = 90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BOF = 90^\circ - 33^\circ = \boxed{57^\circ}$.

Ray OE extends horizontally to the right from O, ray OF extends vertically upward from O, and a right-angle symbol is marked between OE and OF in the figure. Ray OB is located within the region between OE and OF. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOD = 66°. Because AB and CD are intersecting straight lines, ∠AOD and ∠BOC are vertical angles, and vertical angles are equal, therefore ∠BOC = 66°. Also because OE bisects ∠BOC, ∠BOE = 66° ÷ 2 = 33°.
